Swiss-type CNC automatic lathe · 3 m bar feeder · Ø3–20 mm work

How a Swiss-type lathe turns bar into parts

A 3 m bar feeder pushes a long bar into a compact sliding-headstock lathe of the Citizen Cincom kind. Inside, the headstock carries the spinning bar out through a guide bushing, a gang of tools cuts it right at the bushing, and a back spindle takes each finished part away. Both drawings are live: the first runs a whole bar through the feeder, the second makes one pin.

Drawn from the reference photo of a compact Cincom-style machine (light-grey body, door and panel on the left, long dark-grey feeder on two pedestals). Capacity, spindle speed, stroke per chucking and centre height follow published figures for 20 mm Cincom machines such as the A20; the inside is drawn to scale but simplified, and the pin, its program and the feeder details are illustrative.

Sources: Marubeni Citizen-Cincom, A20 · Millennium Machinery, Citizen A20 · Citizen patent US 10,894,292 (guide bushing and headstock) · US 5,564,171 (Swiss-type back spindle)

Anatomy of a CNC lathe

How a slant-bed turning center cuts a part

Follow one block of G-code from the control, through the servo motors and ball screws, to the tool edge and the chips it makes. Hover any part to name it; the numbers follow the figure.

From G-code to chips

  1. ProgramThe control reads one block at a time.—
  2. ControlIt plans the move and sends position commands to the servo amplifiers.—
  3. Servo motorsEach axis motor turns until its encoder reports the commanded position.—
  4. Ball screwsOne turn moves the slide one lead: 12 mm in Z, 10 mm in X.—
  5. Tool cutsThe turning bar meets the insert; the slides feed it along.—
  6. Chips outChips fall down the slant into the conveyor, which lifts them into the bin.—

Thermal compensation

As the spindle runs, the headstock warms and the steel grows about 11.5 µm per metre per °C, pushing the spindle nose toward the tool. Sensors on the headstock feed a model in the control, which offsets the axes by the predicted growth.
